key_insight: A CT-based deep foundation model (CIPHER) can predict which lung cancer patients are at higher risk of immune checkpoint inhibitor–induced pneumonitis before treatment starts.
clinical_relevance: If validated further, this could help clinicians identify patients needing closer monitoring and earlier intervention when starting immunotherapy.
method: Self-supervised pretraining on 590,284 CT slices from 2,500 NSCLC patients using contrastive learning plus a transformer-based masked autoencoder.
Fine-tuned on an internal immunotherapy cohort of 347 patients, with 254 non-ICI-P cases used for training and 93 patients held out for validation.
Compared against clinical, radiomics, and ensemble models, then tested in an external Johns Hopkins cohort.
evidence_signal: CIPHER achieved AUCs of 0.77–0.85 internally, AUC 0.83 in head-to-head benchmarking, and external validation performance of AUC 0.83 with 81.7% balanced accuracy.
watch_item: This is an imaging-based predictive model from retrospective cohorts, so broader prospective validation and workflow integration are still needed before real-world use.
paper_title: CT-Based Deep Foundation Model for Predicting Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Induced Pneumonitis Risk in Lung Cancer
